causal_discovery.guidance: Discovery and independence tests under explicit assumptions; retain equivalence classes and orientation uncertainty.
Model and test the discovered or supplied assumptions; DoWhy is not a general causal discovery algorithm.

causal_modelling.guidance: Represent explicit causal graphs and mechanisms; model adequacy and assumptions need separate evidence.

causal_identification.guidance: Identify effects from an explicit graph and estimand; preserve unidentifiable results and assumptions.

causal_estimation.guidance: Estimate only an identified estimand with declared treatment, population, confounding assumptions and uncertainty.

causal_testing.guidance: Use refutation or graph falsification for the stated assumptions; passing a test does not prove causal validity.

abductive.guidance: Posterior or MAP queries over supplied finite hypotheses, priors, conditional probability tables and observations; retain candidate-set and likelihood-model adequacy obligations and impossible evidence. Do not invent hypotheses or priors or treat the highest posterior as causal proof.

inductive.guidance: Statistical estimation, tests and uncertainty for explicitly sampled observations; retain population, trial identities, exclusions and sampling assumptions. Do not substitute another interval for an authored Wilson bound or refresh source observation times.

Use only when the operation requires predictive fitting or validation, with declared features, split identities, leakage controls and held-out observations. Training fit does not establish generalisation, sampling adequacy or causality.

counterfactual.guidance: Use gcm.counterfactual_samples with a supplied structural causal model and the same factual exogenous context under the intervention. Observed-data noise reconstruction requires invertible mechanisms; otherwise supply justified noise data. Interventional samples or predictive feature recourse are not individual counterfactuals; retain model adequacy obligations.

statistical_inference.guidance: Statistical estimators and tests with explicit sampling design, units, uncertainty and numerical limits.
Statistical model fitting and diagnostics; retain model/design assumptions and uncertainty.

formal_verification.guidance: SMT over an authored formalisation with explicit solver bounds; unknown or timeout is not proof.
Symbolic calculations under explicit domains and assumptions; symbolic output alone is not a proof certificate.

probabilistic_inference.guidance: Bayesian-model inference over supplied hypotheses, graph, priors, likelihoods and observations; do not invent them.

similarity.guidance: Authored feature distances or nearest neighbours; retain feature scaling and separate transfer/applicability review.

optimisation.guidance: Use scipy.optimize for an authored objective and constraints; retain solver status, tolerances and exhausted computation.

causal_discovery.guidance: PC discovery under explicit assumptions; preserve ambiguous orientations and do not substitute for general causal identification.

causal_modelling.guidance: Explicit DAG/functional mechanisms, sampling and interventions; mechanism fit does not establish external validity.

abductive.guidance: Distribution PMF or interval-mass primitives for an explicitly supplied finite hypothesis and observation model; preserve priors, alternatives, uncertainty and a nonzero finite evidence normaliser. A density is not a probability mass. This is not a hypothesis-discovery or Bayesian-network engine.

inductive.guidance: Statistical summaries and distribution functions for declared samples, populations and uncertainty; retain trial identities and exclusions. Do not replace native Wilson-count semantics with another interval or treat a fitted model as sampling-design validation.

counterfactual.guidance: Linear-algebra primitives only for a supplied bounded affine structural causal model with fixed factual exogenous context. Replace the intervened structural equation, preserve the other mechanisms, and reject singular, nonfinite or unsupported systems. No causal identification, generic SCM engine or invented model; retain numerical tolerances and model adequacy obligations.

statistical_inference.guidance: Distributions, statistical functions and tests under an explicit sampling design; retain numerical and uncertainty limits.

formal_verification.guidance: Propositional CNF SAT only; use a separately prepared SMT solver if the operation needs arithmetic or quantifiers.

probabilistic_inference.guidance: Distribution and likelihood primitives only; not a Bayesian-network or general abduction engine.

similarity.guidance: Nearest-neighbour and distance calculations over authored features; similarity does not qualify an analogy.

optimisation.guidance: LP/MIP modelling with an explicitly prepared solver backend; default features need external CBC; retain solver status.

causal_discovery.guidance: Time-series SURD/SCIC/VarSelect operations under their stated assumptions; not a general DoWhy identification/refutation substitute.

abductive.guidance: Distribution probability-mass or interval-mass primitives for supplied finite hypotheses, priors and observation models; retain candidate-set adequacy and require a nonzero finite evidence normaliser. Densities are not probability masses. No automatic hypothesis discovery or Bayesian-network engine.

inductive.guidance: Statistical summaries and estimators for declared samples and populations; retain original trial identities, exclusions, sampling assumptions and uncertainty. Native Wilson-count semantics and authored acceptance criteria remain unchanged.

counterfactual.guidance: Matrix primitives only for a supplied bounded affine structural causal model with fixed factual exogenous context. Replace the intervened equation; require a square full-rank system and reject conditioning, nonfinite or unsupported-model failures. Never use least-squares output to resolve an unidentified causal model. No general causal engine.
